GameName
Integration identifier for telemetry grouping (e.g. "tryll-roleplay-demo"). Leave empty to omit; the server defaults to the project name, then "unknown", when telemetry is on. Pass UTryllRuntimeSettings::GameName to drive this from the project settings asset.
Locale
Session language as a BCP-47 tag (e.g. "de", "pt-BR"). See UTryllRuntimeSettings::Locale for everything it drives. Empty uses the project setting unless bUseProjectLocaleWhenEmpty is false; a malformed tag is rejected with InvalidLocale (2004).
bUseProjectLocaleWhenEmpty
When true, an empty Locale adopts the text provider's current language, then UTryllRuntimeSettings::Locale. Set false with an empty Locale to explicitly disable session language. The four engine parameters this took through protocol v12 are gone. The engine set is derived from the models registered in UTryllModelManifest — each model's catalog entry already states which engine runs it, so there is nothing for a caller to choose, and nothing that can drift out of step with the models the project references.
Storage root is process-wide (set when the server launches via storage-root), not per session — protocol v24 removed CreateSessionRequest.storage_data_folder.
Change the session language without tearing the session down. Pass an empty Locale to clear it.

Applies to every agent, existing and future, from its next turn: TTS language and the locale template keys are read per turn, not captured at agent creation. A new voice input picks up the new STT language hint; one already open keeps its recognizer. Storage paths re-resolve on the next load, but content already bound to a node (a Retrieve KB, canned lines) does NOT swap - those params are structural, so switching authored content still means recreating agents.
Not turn-atomic: a turn already running may render its prompt under the old locale and synthesize under the new one.
Completion is broadcast via OnSetSessionLocaleComplete.

Tell Tryll the text provider's language changed (custom providers call this). Sends SetSessionLocale unless CreateSession was given an explicit locale, then re-resolves Localized prompts on live agents. Also reaches the editor session.

Report how hard the server should yield the GPU back to the game (the manual inference throttle knob). Fire-and-forget: no response, no error surfaced locally. Never sent automatically — a session that never calls this runs unthrottled.
Level
0 = full speed (default), 1 = maximum yielding. Clamped server-side; out-of-range values do not fail here.

Record + verify the server identity advertised in ConnectionReady. When bAutoLaunchServer is enabled this subsystem owns the server's lifecycle, so a mismatch is fail-closed: logs an error and disconnects. Otherwise (an explicit external connection) a mismatch is advisory-only. Returns false if the mismatch caused a fail-closed disconnect — the caller must not proceed with CreateSession in that case.

True when a shared UTryllEditorSubsystem exists to route through instead of this instance's own Connection (editor process, GEditor available — PIE and editor tool windows). False for packaged/player builds and for commandlets running with GEditor == nullptr, both of which keep the full local implementation below as their only implementation. Resolved fresh on every call, never cached, matching LaunchServerProcess()'s existing discipline.
Any of OnToolCall / OnToolCallWithId / OnToolCallDetailed is bound. Such a listener can answer a paused tool-call batch with ResumeWithToolResult(s).

briefdescription.para: Embedding ClassifyIntent — event_type="intent_classified". Subscribing swallows OnNodeEvent.

detaileddescription.para: Detailed tool-call event carrying the full owning FTryllToolCall value object (node name and disposition included) alongside the agent id. Fired in addition to — never instead of — OnToolCall / OnToolCallWithId, so a manual handler can tell whether to send results for await_result or plain-resume for other pausing dispositions. ClassifyIntentLLM — event_type="intent_llm_classified". Subscribing swallows OnNodeEvent. Pause typed event — fired for NodeEvent event_type="paused" (the executor paused the turn between nodes; ChangeAgentParam is allowed while paused). Generic NodeEvent fallback — fired for any event_type without a typed delegate (or when the typed delegate has no subscribers). KvPairs preserves wire order. Game-instance subsystem: one TCP session to the Tryll server. Manages the socket connection on a background thread (FTryllConnection) and drains the event queue on Tick(), dispatching to registered agents and delegates.

Default (zero-wiring) path — driven by UTryllRuntimeSettings:
bAutoLaunchServer → spawns the bundled tryll_server.exe on Initialize.
bAutoConnect → Connect() on Initialize (connect-retry covers server startup).
bAutoCreateSession → on Connected, CreateSessionFromSettings() sends the game name, locale and the manifest-derived engine hint. UTryllAgentComponent / UTryllVoiceInputComponent then create themselves once IsSessionReady() — they queue until OnCreateSessionComplete if they spawn earlier. So the common case is: download models in the Model Manager, add the components, press play. There is no engine to pick: each model's catalog entry names it.

Manual path — turn those flags off to drive the session yourself:
Connect() — open TCP session to ServerHost:ServerPort.
OnConnectionChanged(bConnected=true) — bind to continue; or poll IsConnected().
CreateSession(GameName, Locale) — configure explicitly (overrides settings). Completion arrives on OnCreateSessionComplete; IsSessionReady() is true thereafter.
CreateAgent — attach a UTryllAgentComponent (auto-creates once the session is ready) or call RequestCreateAgent().
SendMessage(Text) — drive one turn; chunks on OnAnswerText, the turn ends with OnTurnComplete(Status).
RequestDestroyAgent / Disconnect — tear down when done.
All delegates fire on the game thread from Tick(); it is safe to touch UObjects and UI directly from callbacks.
